title: Listed company exposure to government budget functions, South Africa
basis: Each entry states a mechanical link between a consolidated expenditure function in static_data/gov_budget_SA.json and a company that exists in static_data/listing_JSE.json. The link is a channel, not a forecast. No entry says a company will earn more, and no entry is a recommendation.

directness_definitions.direct: The company's product or service is paid for with money from this function, or the company holds contracts the function pays for.
directness_definitions.indirect: The channel runs through an intermediate party, a state owned entity's operating budget, or costs and demand.

sources.document: Budget Review 2026, National Treasury, Republic of South Africa, 25 February 2026
sources.used_for: The expenditure functions and their amounts, Table 5.4 and Table 1.5.
figures: consolidated expenditure by function FY2025/26 and FY2026/27

sources.document: static_data/listing_JSE.json, read directly from the working tree of this repository
sources.used_for: The universe of securities. Every code in this file was checked against it, and the checker re-checks on every run.

direct.reason: Wilson Bayly Holmes-Ovcon is a construction group; provincial education departments fund school building and upgrade programmes from this function, and contractors are paid from that vote.
Raubex is a construction and materials group; school and post-school infrastructure funded from this function is built by contractors.

indirect.reason: Novus Holdings is a printing and packaging group; school book and workbook print runs are funded from education budgets.

direct.reason: Aspen Pharmacare manufactures generic medicines in South Africa; public hospitals funded from this function purchase medicines through provincial and national procurement.

indirect.reason: Wilson Bayly Holmes-Ovcon builds hospital infrastructure; the function funds hospital construction and refurbishment.

Old Mutual administers and manages retirement fund assets; social security funds and public-sector pensions are transferred out of this function into funds whose assets are managed by regulated asset managers.
Sanlam manages retirement fund assets; the social security and pension transfers in this function are invested through regulated managers.
Momentum Group administers and manages retirement fund assets in the same market.

direct.reason: Wilson Bayly Holmes-Ovcon is a construction group; the economic regulation and infrastructure sub-function funds road, rail, water and port works that contractors are paid to build.
Raubex is a road construction and materials group; the roads programme inside the infrastructure sub-function pays contractors directly.
Aveng is a construction and engineering group; state infrastructure contracts in this function are its customer base.
PPC makes cement; the infrastructure works funded here consume cement.
Sephaku Holdings owns a cement producer; the same infrastructure works consume cement.
Afrimat supplies aggregates and construction materials; road and civil works funded here consume aggregates.
Brikor makes bricks and clay products; publicly funded building works consume them.

indirect.reason: Sasol produces liquid fuels and chemicals; state owned transport and power entities funded under this function are large fuel and feedstock customers, but the money reaches Sasol through their operating budgets, not directly from the vote.
Exxaro supplies coal; state owned power generation funded under this function is a customer, at one remove.
Thungela exports and supplies coal; domestic power generation funded under this function is a customer, at one remove.

cross_cutting.label: Government borrowing and the banking sector
cross_cutting.note: Debt-service costs of R432.4 billion in FY 2026/27 are a charge on the consolidated budget outside the function rows. Banks hold and trade the government bonds through which that debt is funded.
companies: Standard Bank Group is a bank; South African banks hold government bonds as part of their investment book.
Absa Group is a bank; it holds government bonds as part of its investment book.
FirstRand is a bank; it holds government bonds as part of its investment book.
Nedbank Group is a bank; it holds government bonds as part of its investment book.
Capitec Bank is a bank; it holds government bonds as part of its liquid asset portfolio.
Investec is a bank and asset manager; it holds and trades government bonds.

source.document: Budget Review 2026, National Treasury, Republic of South Africa, 25 February 2026

excluded.reason: Shoprite sells food to households. No function in the budget buys retail food.
MTN sells connectivity to retail and enterprise customers. Government is a customer through many departments, but no single function can be shown to carry that revenue.
Kumba Iron Ore sells iron ore to steelmakers and export markets. No budget function is its customer.

notes: Construction names appear under both Learning and culture and Economic development because school building and road building are paid from two different functions, which is two different money.
The map is thin by design. Where a function's money goes to households (social grants, payments for financial assets) no company can be mechanically placed against it.
